# A `#id` may be duplicated; a handle that is *read* may not be rendered twice.
#
# uniqueNodeIDs renames the later copies of an id and lets the first keep the
# name, so a test naming `#inc` still means the `#inc` it wrote. A read cannot
# follow that rename: the checker declares one var per written id and every
# spliced copy of that body shares it, so `bar.pulse()` in each copy resolves to
# the first copy's field. The second widget is created and then never touched.
#
# Before ir.Var.NodeHandle the same program emitted a bare `bar` and cgo said
# `undefined: bar` -- loudly wrong. Qualifying the read is what would have made
# it quietly wrong, so the duplicate is refused in the pass that first knows of
# it rather than left to the host compiler to miss.
#
# The rename is keyed by name and the refusal by symbol, and they are different
# questions: the rename repairs the emitted namespace, where any two `#bar`s
# collide, while the refusal is about a read that cannot say which copy it
# meant, which only arises within one body. innocent.sngl is the difference.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out dup.sngl
stderr 'is read here, and .* renders more than one of it'

# The diagnostic names the read, not just the node: the remedies it offers are
# actionable where the read is written, and a user landing on the node sees
# nothing wrong there.
! sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out1 dup.sngl
stderr 'dup\.sngl:15:9'

# Two unrelated components may each write `#bar`. `reader` is rendered once and
# is the only thing that reads it; `quiet` is rendered twice and reads nothing.
# Neither var satisfies both halves, so this compiles. Keyed by name it was
# refused -- and the message then asserted that a component rendered once
# renders more than one.
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out2 innocent.sngl
grep 'C\.gtk_progress_bar_pulse\(m\.bar\)' out2/model.go
grep 'bar__1 ' out2/model.go
grep 'bar__2 ' out2/model.go

# The same program with `quiet`'s id spelled differently. This is the pair that
# keeps the keying honest: the two differ only in a name that `reader`'s read was
# never bound to, so a symbol-keyed refusal cannot tell them apart and both
# compile. If a future change rejoins the two by spelling, exactly one of this
# pair goes red.
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out3 renamed.sngl
grep 'C\.gtk_progress_bar_pulse\(m\.bar\)' out3/model.go
grep 'baz ' out3/model.go
grep 'baz__1 ' out3/model.go

# One instance is the ordinary case: the handle is the Model's field, and the
# native receiver reaches it.
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out4 single.sngl
grep 'C\.gtk_progress_bar_pulse\(m\.bar\)' out4/model.go

-- dup.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import "sngl:platform/gtk4"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

component bump() node {
    gtk4.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}

    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
        bar.pulse()
    })
}

window {
    vbox {
        bump()
        bump()
    }
}
-- innocent.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import "sngl:platform/gtk4"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

component reader() node {
    gtk4.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}

    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
        bar.pulse()
    })
}

component quiet() node {
    gtk4.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.5) {}
}

window {
    vbox {
        reader()
        quiet()
        quiet()
    }
}
-- renamed.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import "sngl:platform/gtk4"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

component reader() node {
    gtk4.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}

    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
        bar.pulse()
    })
}

component quiet() node {
    gtk4.GtkProgressBar #baz(fraction=0.5) {}
}

window {
    vbox {
        reader()
        quiet()
        quiet()
    }
}
-- single.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import "sngl:platform/gtk4"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

window {
    vbox {
        gtk4.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}
        time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
            bar.pulse()
        })
    }
}
